core_obligations: Reduce to an affine open and get surjectivity: for U = Spec(B) an affine open of X put A = Gamma(U, A); since H^1(U, I) = 0 the map A -> B = Gamma(U, O_X) is surjective, and by assumption I = I(U) is an ideal of square zero in A (proof lines 112-117).

Show (U, A|_U) is affine: use the canonical morphism (U, A|_U) -> Spec(A) associated with B -> Gamma(U, A), note that it fits into the displayed commutative square with (U, O_X|_U) -> Spec(B), and conclude that it is a homeomorphism on underlying topological spaces, so that it suffices to check it is an isomorphism on local rings (proof lines 118-134).

Finish the local check: for u in U with prime p in A, use the displayed commutative diagram of short exact sequences comparing 0 -> I_p -> A_p -> B_p -> 0 with 0 -> I_u -> A_u -> O_{X,u} -> 0; the outer arrows are isomorphisms because I and O_X are quasi-coherent, hence so is the middle one, so every point of X' = (X, A) has an affine neighbourhood and X' is a scheme with X -> X' a first order thickening (proof lines 135-153).
proof_roadmap: Pass to an affine open U = Spec(B), observe H^1(U, I) = 0 so that A -> B is surjective, and record that I = I(U) has square zero (proof lines 112-117).

Use the functoriality of Spec to obtain (U, A|_U) -> Spec(A), compare it with (U, O_X|_U) -> Spec(B) and reduce the claim that it is an isomorphism to a statement about local rings (proof lines 118-134).

Compare the two short exact sequences of local rings in the displayed square; quasi-coherence of I and O_X makes the outer arrows isomorphisms, hence the middle one too, so X' is a scheme (proof lines 135-153).
difficulty_reason: The lemma characterises first order thickenings over a base algebraically: a short exact sequence 0 -> I -> A -> O_X -> 0 of sheaves on X with A a sheaf of f^{-1}O_S-algebras, I of square zero and I quasi-coherent as an O_X-module makes X' = (X, A) a scheme and X -> X' a first order thickening over S, and every first order thickening arises this way (statement lines 93-108). The substance is the local computation: on an affine open U = Spec(B) the vanishing of H^1(U, I) makes A = Gamma(U, A) -> B surjective, and the candidate isomorphism (U, A|_U) -> Spec(A) has to be checked on local rings, which is done by comparing two short exact sequences whose outer arrows are isomorphisms precisely because I and O_X are quasi-coherent (proof lines 112-150). The author leaves the converse direction implicit and it is reproduced as written. The claim is H2: a genuine local-ring computation with one vanishing input, not a citation.
